decisions.reason: As a newly launched classic handle in the firm’s core business, it is cheap to keep in the catalog and there is not yet enough evidence to justify abandonment.
A door lever handle family fits the established product portfolio, and a large German metal-products firm would usually keep such a recent low-cost option open while market response becomes clearer.
A new door handle design carries some style risk, but after only one year the uncertainty is still unresolved and the cost of maintaining it is likely modest.
This design variant is still an early-stage option in the firm’s core market, so management would likely continue observing demand rather than exit immediately.
As another handle family closely related to the firm’s main business, it likely has low ongoing carrying costs and retains option value after a short time on the market.

The electronic access system is more uncertain and likely costlier to support than mechanical handles, but its strategic potential and very recent launch make continued market presence the more likely choice for now.
